recipes.name: Slow Cooker Apple Butter
ingredients_raw: 12 pounds Golden Delicious apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Place apples and vinegar into a large slow cooker and cover with the lid. Cook on High for 8 hours, then turn to Low and continue cooking for 10 more hours.
Stir in white sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, allspice, and cloves. Cook on Low for 4 more hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Apple Butter
raw_recipe.description: This apple butter cooks unattended for hours in a slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: Went by the recipe & used tart apples.I did add the sugar in the last couple of hours of cooking which was done by taste.I think I used about half of what the recipe called for.Turned out GREAT husband & family loved it as well as my co workers.This one will be in my recipe box for years to come!!

Like many of the others here, I liked the recipe, but with changes. I used an equal mix of 4 tart apple varieties—Pink Lady, Stayman Winesap, Granny Smith, and Arkansas Black. I cut the sugar way down--1 cup each of white and brown. However, I kept the spices exactly the same. Their flavor is strong but I liked it. You may wish to cut down. Not sure if your ratios will work the same, but for me, 1 pound of whole apples equaled one cup of finished product. I used 10 pounds of apples and my yield was 10 cups of apple butter. Also like the others, I did not need to cook it quite as long as the recipe states. For me, it was 6 hours on high, 9 hours on low, then added the sugar and spices and kept on low for 2 hours more with the lid off to make thicker. I used an immersion blender after the first 6 hours to make it smooth. I then canned the butter using a 10 minute hot water bath. It looks great and tastes awesome and I plan to give out as Christmas gifts.

Love making this every year. It doesn't matter what kind of apples you use, it's especially good when you mix the varieties. Plus, you don't need to use nearly that amount of sugar. I use a large crock pot and end up using 1/2 cup of white and 1/2 cup of brown sugar. I also use 1 Tsp of cloves and 1 TB each of Cinnamon and All Spice. But put a little in and stir and cook a little and then taste it. Everyone's tastes are different. I also use an immersion blender and it makes it nice and smooth. I end up cooking mine a lot longer on low and then turn it back to high at the end when I'm ready to can it. You just need to boil the jars for 5 minutes and let them sit in the water for 5 minutes to finish up. It's a great gift for the holidays too!

I made this with Golden Delicious. I followed the directions mostly, but I left out one cup of white sugar. I figured I'd add it later if need be, but it wasn't needed! I have a sweet tooth and this is great as is!! (I used 1c brown and 2c white sugar) I have a 6qt crockpot and it couldn't hold all 12lb of apples. I was able to just barely fit 3/4 I'd them so I simmered the last 1/4 on the stove top for about 20minutes, in 2T of apple cider vinegar and put 6T of acv in the crockpot. Once the stove top apples were mush, I was able to fit them in the crockpot. My crock cooks hot so I kept it on high for 4 hours before going to bed and left it on warm overnight (about 9 hours). In the morning, it looked awesome so I kept it on low all morning (another 6 hours). Then I added the spices and sugar and set it on low for 4 hours. It was a bit thinner than I wanted so I took the lid off and left it on low another hour. I pureed in a blender and water bath canned it (10min in boiling water, 5 min to rest off heat, remove from pot and don't touch for 12 hours). It thickened up as it cooled and it's FANTASTIC!!! I could, and have, just eaten it from the jar. All total, it made 7.5 pints! I canned it in half pint jars, and had 15! The ones not eaten by myself and kids will be gifts for Christmas. It's amazing stuff!!

This is the best recipe! It is very forgiving as well! First I am not the greatest cook, and I can't bake at all, but for some reason I am taken with making jams and canning, I came across this recipe as I was looking for something for valentine gifts for friends at church - You are the apple of my eye - be mine kind of thing... While this takes a long time to make, it tastes fabulous and after all those hours, imagine my dismay when I accidently put a table spoon of cloves instead if a teaspoon! I almost cried! but I just scraped it up and moved on....It tastes fantastic!- I too changed a few things. I used gala and pink lady apples since 3 pound bags were on sale this week. I only used 1 cup of white sugar and 1 cup of brown, it's sweet enough, but not overly - next time, I'm going to try it with 1/2 cup of the sugars. I left the skin on and just cut the apples up small and after I had to go to work so I shut the cooker off and let it sit while I went to work, when I came home, ran the apples through my vita mix to make it smooth - and wow is it smooth. I then was able to put the butter in a smaller slow cooker add the spices (and scrape my mistake out) stir it up and put the slow cooker on low for the final 4 hours with the lid off to make it thicken. Melissa - this is the best recipe! I got 11 - 8oz jars from my batch. This is going to be a perfect valentines day gift for these cold Pittsburgh days. Again, Thank you Melissa!

Excellent recipe. I chose this one because I wanted a little more control over how much sugar I used. Apples vary so much, I felt more comfortable adding to taste after the apples cooked up. I simply filled my slow cooker to the top with peeled, chopped apples and let them cook. When it was time I added a cup of brown sugar and a cup of regular. Later, after pureeing in my food processor, I tasted and added another cup of regular sugar and then let it cook the final hour. The cooking time was exact. I'm really impressed that it came out so exact as I expected it to be something I'd have to feel out a bit. I'm also really pleased with the spices. They are just right!

Quantity: Measured out 12 lbs of Cortland apples which are sweet/tart. All but two apples fit in my large slow cooker. Yielded 6 pint jars of apple butter. 
Sweetness: Cut the white sugar in half and used a scant cup of dark brown sugar. I think it's a good sweetness, though I may cut the white sugar a little more if I make again. 
Consistency: It was still pretty soupy after the 22 hours of cooking so I gave it another 20-30 minutes on high with the lid off. I also processed about half through a food mill. If my immersion blender were working, I would have used that, as the Cortland apples produced a slightly more textured puree than I wanted. I'm happy with the consistency now.
Spice: It's a fairly standard apple butter spice combo, perhaps a little on the strong side. I'm not so taken with it that it will keep me from experimenting and tweaking. I don't understand how someone could not like apple butter but like this apple butter unless it's the slightly stronger spice taste they are responding to.

I used only two cups of white sugar and no brown sugar. I added a tablespoon of butter with the spices and cooked it the last 8 hours with a cheesecloth covering the crock pot under the lid. This absorbed the evaporating liquid and helped it cook down. I got 9 half pint jars out of this batch. Yum! Thank you for the great recipe!

My crock-pot only held 6 1/2 lbs of apples. I cooked them with 1/4 C of Apple cider Vinegar until very soft, and then since I didn't peel the apples, I ran them through my food mill. Returned to the crock-pot with 1 C white sugar, 1 t. cinnamon, 1/4 t. pumpkin spice (since I didn't have ground cloves) and 1/2 t. allspice. It tastes great, but I'm letting the flavors blend into the butter and will check it again in a while to make sure I don't need to adjust the spices or sugar.

This is my first time attempting to make apple butter, and it couldn't have been easier! I used a bag full of apples that we got from a friend, so they were mixed... mostly granny smith, but some golden delicious and gala. I did change the sweetener to 1c honey, 1c white sugar, and 1c brown sugar. It left the butter a bit tart (which we like). But overall, this was simple to make and turned out delicious! Also, ran the immersion blender through it right before I turned it to low.

I am amazed at how well this worked, I was certain I would have to put the apple mixture through the blender to get the chunks out, but there were none there. I also had the problem of very sweet apple butter; but I've never eaten it or made it before and I'm not sure how sweet it is supposed to be. I did use sweet apples, as that's what I had from our apple tree but I put in less half the amount of sugar. The other thing is that I expected it to make a lot more, I was going to do it for Christmas presents, but I only got 4 pint jars (barely). I didn't have quite enough room in my crock pot for 12 pounds of apples, but I did 10. I cooked it for as long as it said and if I make it again (it was a lot of time to put in for only 4 jars) I will cook it for less time and less moisture will evaporate from it.

Didn't use the vinegar. I used 1 1/2 c. white and 1/2 c brown sugar. Added 1 T. cinnamon, 1 tea. each nutmeg and cloves and 1/2 t. allspice. The first time I used a mix of cortland and rome..this was the best, the next time stayman and rome. Still very good but had more juice so it is a little more runny but still very great. can't believe how easy and delicious.

Great flavor. I made a half recipe and cut the sugar by half. I skipped the ground cloves (didn’t have any) but it didn’t affect th3 flavor. Be advised the cooking time was half what the recipe indicated, although I did let it cook down for a total of 3 hours to reach the consistency I wanted. Made 4.5 pints. Finished with water bath canning so I can give away for the holidays!
This is the 4th year I have made this apple butter. My family loves it. Last year I made 2 batches. I suggest you go slow adding the sugar, it usually doesn't need it all.
Husband loves different “butters” so I substituted plums/- turned out great!
I did not peel my apples as I don’t mind the extra textures. Very easy to make and tastes divine. Definitely will be making this again

Originally it was so sweet, had to throw it out. Tried it the second time & I left out the cider vinegar. I put only 1/2 cup of brown sugar & it came out delicious! The apples all ready are naturally sweet so by cutting the sugar down really brought out the apple flavor. You can always add more sugar for your personal taste.
Very easy and delicious

I actually completed mine in the Instant Pot. I also crushed pecans and added them from the beginning so that they would soften and cook the flavor into the apples. Friends & family cannot get enough!
The hardest part is peeling the apples. It is really good. I like it better than store bought. I’ve made it several times.
